words.meaning: To shorten a piece of writing while keeping its main points.
words.example: The teacher gave students an abridged version of the novel to read over the holidays.

words.meaning: To decorate something to make it more beautiful.
words.example: The students used colorful ribbons to adorn the hall for the festival.

words.meaning: Able to move quickly and easily.
words.example: The agile gymnast leaped across the beam without losing her balance.

words.meaning: To cause pain, trouble, or illness to someone.
words.example: The old sailor refused to say what continued to ail him after the long voyage.

words.meaning: To claim that something is true without giving proof yet.
words.example: The article did not name the manager reporters allege was responsible for the missing funds.

words.meaning: To gather a large amount of something over time.
words.example: The scientist spent decades trying to amass enough data to prove her theory.

words.meaning: The highest point or tip of something.
words.example: The climbers reached the apex of the mountain just before sunset.

words.meaning: Extremely dry, with little or no rainfall.
words.example: Few plants can survive in the arid desert without special adaptations.

words.meaning: To attack someone or something violently, physically or with words.
words.example: Reporters began to assail the minister with questions the moment he stepped outside.

words.meaning: A large number of things, such as questions or blows, coming quickly one after another.
words.example: The coach faced a barrage of criticism after the team lost the final match.

words.meaning: Lacking strong flavor, excitement, or interest; dull.
words.example: The cafeteria food was so bland that students started bringing their own lunches.

words.meaning: To speak loudly and aggressively with little real substance behind it.
words.example: The captain tried to bluster his way out of the argument instead of admitting the foul.

words.meaning: A terrible event that causes great damage or suffering; a disaster.
words.example: The flood was a calamity that destroyed half the crops in the village.

words.meaning: A process in which something happens in stages, one after another, often quickly.
words.example: One error in the code caused a cascade of failures throughout the entire system.

words.meaning: To scold someone gently for doing something wrong.
words.example: The coach began to chide the players for arriving late to practice.

words.meaning: Done secretly, often because it is not allowed.
words.example: The students held a clandestine meeting after hours to plan the surprise party.

words.meaning: To come together to form one single group or thing.
words.example: The scattered clubs decided to coalesce into a single student council.

words.meaning: Aware of or having knowledge of something.
words.example: The manager was fully cognizant of the risks before approving the new plan.

words.meaning: To praise someone officially for something they did well.
words.example: The principal decided to commend the students for their outstanding project.

words.meaning: Involved with others in a wrongful act.
words.example: The employee claimed he was not complicit in the plan to falsify the records.
